facts.text: Quadraspherical Plasma Analyzer was deployed at Interstellar Trajectory — Aldebaran & Aquila during Pioneer 10 & 11 in 1972.
Electrostatic curved-plate analyzer designed by John Wolfe to count solar wind protons, electrons, and interstellar ions.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Discovered that the solar wind slows down and interacts with interstellar hydrogen atoms at the outer fringes of the heliosphere.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Interstellar Trajectory — Aldebaran & Aquila.
Mapped the true boundary where the Sun's magnetic realm gives way to the interstellar ocean.
